resources.string: Every bank SMS becomes a transaction waiting for one tap: which category was it?
Sort each payment from the notification or the home-screen widget, in a second.
Clear the inbox every day to keep a streak and see your month at a glance.
No internet permission: your SMS and spending never leave this phone. You can check it in App info.
To find your payments, Budget Widget needs to read SMS. Here is exactly what it does with them:
Only messages from banks and card issuers are looked at. Personal messages are skipped and never stored.
Reading happens on this phone. Nothing is uploaded: the app has no internet access.
Bank messages are kept with their transaction, so you can see where it came from. Delete them any time.
For apps installed outside the Play Store, Android hides SMS access behind an extra switch. To turn it on:
Tap ⋮ (top right), then Allow restricted settings, and confirm.
Tap Permissions, then SMS, then Allow.
A notification shows each new payment with your daily categories (Groceries, Restaurant, Public transport) as buttons. Sort it without opening the app.
Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery, which delays notifications. The app catches up every few hours anyway, but for instant alerts:
In App info, open Battery and choose Unrestricted.
On Samsung, also check Settings, Battery, Background usage limits: Budget Widget must not be under Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps.
Import bank SMS already in your inbox, or start tracking from today.
A month of payments to sort
More history for the charts; more to sort
Importing needs SMS access. You can import later from Settings.
A starter set with subcategories. Rename, add, reorder or archive them any time in the Categories tab.
The Quick-Sort widget shows the next payment with category buttons. Most people sort everything from there.
Long-press your home screen, choose Widgets, and find Budget Widget.
